column1: # REFERENCE TRUTH. Every row below was written by hand from reading the YAML
# under cases/<case>/, NOT produced by tests/acceptance/AUR-361.sh. Nothing in
# this file is a copy of anything the acceptance program generates, so the
# fixture phase compares the derivation against an independent claim instead
#   exit            expected exit of the derivation (0 pass, 1 refuse)
#   code            expected typed code; `pass` when exit is 0
#   active          expected active `uses:` site count  (`-` when exit is 1)
#   inert           expected inert `uses:`-bearing line count (`-` when exit is 1)
#   identities      expected sorted, unique identity list (`-` when exit is 1)
#   reason          expected control that MUST be the one that refused
# WHY THE `reason` COLUMN EXISTS. Round 3 mutation-tested its own controls and
# found that a typed code is NOT enough evidence. Several distinct controls
# share the code `invalid_lock_or_manifest`, so deleting one of them left the
# suite green: a second, redundant control refused with the SAME code and the
# row could not tell the difference. That is the surviving class one level up -
# the check stopped running and nothing observed it. `reason` names the exact
# control, asserted as a colon-delimited field of the refusal detail, so a
# control that stops firing is a red row even when another one masks it.
# No row contains a real or credential-shaped secret. Every commit SHA below
# is a public GitHub Actions release commit already referenced by this repo.
# Round 3 additions. Blocker B1 (docker origin never checked) and blocker B2
# (nested `uses:` inside a local composite action never derived) each get a
# fixture here, hand-written from the YAML under cases/<case>/ exactly like
# every row above. A blocker without a fixture comes back next round.
